title: Apparent sequence-model contribution depends strongly on negative-set construction: analysis code and released evidence
description: A calibration study across 94 paired ENCODE eCLIP datasets. Holding the model class, the peak set, the chromosome-blocked folds and the estimator fixed, refitting model and baseline within each protocol, and varying how negative windows are constructed moves a model's measured nested contribution 4.84-fold under the cross-fitted estimator the paper recommends and reports as primary, and 5.42-fold under the two-stage one this literature uses, while its apparent AUROC moves the opposite way. The two-stage estimator also returns a positive increment for a model whose information the composition baseline already contains, where the true contribution is zero by construction; cross-fitting the covariate removes at least 95 percent of it.
